faq.q: Why can the grayscale PDF be larger than the colour original?
faq.a: True vector grayscale is not possible with the browser PDF library used here, so each page is rendered to an image, converted to grey, and placed into a new PDF. For a document that was mostly text and vector graphics, replacing crisp vectors with a rendered image usually makes the file bigger, not smaller. The tool shows the input and output sizes side by side after conversion so you can decide whether the trade-off is worth it. Photo-heavy pages often shrink; text-only pages usually grow.

faq.q: What is the difference between Grayscale and Pure black & white?
faq.a: Grayscale keeps the full range of greys using the standard luminance formula (0.299 red + 0.587 green + 0.114 blue), which looks natural for photos and shaded diagrams. Pure black & white pushes every pixel to either black or white at a threshold you set with the slider, which gives clean, high-contrast output for text and line art and the smallest ink use on a mono printer. Grayscale pages are saved as JPEG inside the PDF; black-and-white pages are saved as PNG.

faq.q: Does 'Keep text searchable' really keep the text?
faq.a: Yes. With that box ticked, the tool reads each page's text positions and draws them onto the new page as an invisible text layer (render mode 3, fully transparent) sitting over the grey image. You see the picture, but search and copy still find the words. It uses the built-in Helvetica font, which can only encode Latin-1 characters, so anything outside that range — Devanagari, many symbols — is skipped from the hidden layer while the visible image is unaffected.

faq.q: Will my pages stay the right size and orientation, and is the file uploaded?
faq.a: Each output page is created at the original page's displayed size and respects its rotation, so a landscape or rotated page is not turned sideways and the dimensions match the input. DPI (150, 200 or 300) controls how sharp the rendered image is and how big the file gets. All of the rendering and PDF building happens in your browser with pdf.js and pdf-lib; the document is never sent to a server. Pages are processed one at a time with a progress bar and a Cancel button.
